key_insight: Making BaTiO3 membranes thinner suppresses visible cracking, but the thinnest films trade cracking for dense nanoscale wrinkling, so thickness controls a fracture–morphology balance.
engineering_relevance: The results provide practical thickness-selection guidelines for integrating freestanding ferroelectric oxide membranes into silicon-compatible low-power electronic and memory devices.
method: Varied BaTiO3 membrane thickness from 15 nm to 5 nm after release.
Adjusted polymer support thickness for 10 nm membranes to tune wrinkling.
Used piezoresponse force microscopy to track post-release ferroelectric contrast evolution.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports that 5 nm BaTiO3 suppresses large-area visible cracking, while 10 nm membranes show polymer-thickness-dependent wrinkle density and time-dependent PFM contrast after release.
watch_item: Apparent ferroelectric performance may be confounded by morphology changes, charge screening, interfacial contact, and strain relaxation after release.
paper_title: Thickness-dependent crack suppression and wrinkle formation in freestanding BaTiO3 membranes
